rulers.name: Bolko I (with his brother Casimir of Bytom to 1284)

ledger.x: 1172: after a long dispute the Duchy of Opole is formed under Duke Jarosław.
1201: Jarosław dies and Opole falls back to Silesia.
1210: Mieszko Tanglefoot takes Kraków and the High Duke's title.
1211: Mieszko dies and Kraków passes back to Leszek the White.
1234: Henry the Bearded gives Kalisz and Wieluń to Casimir's sons.
1234: Henry the Bearded takes full control of Opole-Racibórz as guardian of Casimir I's sons.
1239: Kalisz and Wieluń go back to Silesia.
1241: Władysław receives Kalisz from Henry II.
1244: Władysław is forced out of Kalisz.
1281: Racibórz is split off again after Duke Władysław's death.
1281: the Duchy of Bytom is established beside the recreated Opole.
1284: Casimir's share is formally divided from Opole.
17 January 1291: Opole's duke does homage to the Bohemian crown.
1304: last year of Cliopatria's Opole shape, not the end of the duchy.

wars.name: Mieszko Tanglefoot's conquest of Opole
wars.outcome: Mieszko Tanglefoot of Racibórz takes Opole in a surprise attack at the beginning of 1202 and merges it with his duchy.

wars.name: Mieszko Tanglefoot's seizure of Kraków
wars.outcome: Mieszko takes Kraków without fighting in 1210 and holds it until his death on 16 May 1211, after which Leszek the White returns.

wars.name: Henry I the Bearded's Kraków campaign
wars.outcome: Unsuccessful: Henry's expedition against Kraków failed, with Opole-Racibórz troops taking part.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Poland
wars.outcome: The Mongols raid Silesia in 1241 and defeat Henry II the Pious at Legnica on 9 April; Mieszko II fights part of them at Racibórz in March; no land changes hands.

wars.name: Konrad of Masovia's 1243 bid for Kraków
wars.outcome: Mieszko II supports his father-in-law Konrad I of Masovia against Kraków; their forces are defeated and no ground is won.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is given on any of the five pages; the duchy is a set of named castellanies and towns (Opole, Racibórz, Cieszyn, Bytom, Kalisz, Wieluń).
